**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-replication.html#/part-4-multiverse-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 opens on the chart that the class has just built and closes on the single analysis you would defend if you had to pick one. The reading on the specification curve is its companion.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd) and slides | Read the exploratory dots from the class against the curve of 864 specifications, and find your own among them. | 10 minutes |
| Slides | Bet on which decision moves estimates most before the decomposition is shown. On the curve of the claim the decomposition attributes the largest share of the variation across specifications to the estimator, the choice between comparing each country with itself after the change shared by all countries in a year has been removed and comparing it with itself including that change. Then where the five reanalyses and the original study are placed on the curve, and what the options that left the curve would do to it. | 16 minutes |
| `try_spec()` on the [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) page | Rerun the specification you submitted, then read off your own placement, the share of the 864 specifications on the curve that lie further in the direction of the claim than your estimate, and send it when the facilitator says go. Without a submission of your own, use the reproduced specification instead. | 7 minutes |
| Slides, the multiverse tutorial and what the curve leaves out | Optional depth on where the idea came from and what a multiverse is for, followed by a slide that is always shown, on the four things that a curve leaves out. | 10 minutes |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) and slides | Why hundreds of estimates on the same data are not hundreds of independent tests, what a curve-level permutation test would have to do, and how to read one if it were run. Then the discussion, argued in chat or at the table. | 12 minutes |
| Slides, with [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) as the follow-up | The three critical positions on multiverse analysis, the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis, what preregistration settles and what it leaves open, and the OSF pages that hold the materials of the case. | 10 minutes |
| The report skeleton in the workspace, or [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) Task 5 | Complete the preregistration block before you run anything, translate the specification in the block into model syntax yourself, run it, and submit with `report_result()`. Your declared result is drawn on the chart as a filled circle beside the open circles of the exploratory round. | 20 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd) | Wrap up with the chart on screen: two points from the literature, and the reminder that the path you declared was one choice among the alternatives you had just seen. | 5 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have your own placement among the 864 specifications of the curve, one specification fixed in the preregistration block of your report before it was run, and a report of your own that contains the result of that specification.
